pre: Welcome to the Harbor Grand Prix, live from Pratt Street!
Engines warming up, and the stoops are packed three deep!
On the grid: one grandpa toad and a field of very nervous drivers.
Hairpin by the Convention Center is gonna eat somebody's tires.
Mavis is in the pit lane with a thermos and a stern look.
Lights are coming on... and they're GONE!
mid: Down the straight past the ballpark, flat out!
Harold dives inside! Bold move for a toad with a cane!
Side by side through the harbor turn, nobody's lifting!
Sparks off the curb! That car's held together with hope!
Into the hairpin, brakes glowing like crab-pot coals!
A slipstream pass on Pratt! The crowd's on its feet!
Halfway done, and the lead has changed four times!
Water taxi horns blasting from the harbor! They love it!
crash: OH! Into the barriers! He's okay, the car is not!
Spin at the hairpin! Somebody tell him which way is forward!
Tire's gone! That wheel is headed for the harbor!
Big bump! A traffic cone just flew over the grandstand!
finish: Final lap! The whole harbor is holding its breath!
Out of the last corner, pedal to the floor!
CHECKERED FLAG! Harold the toad wins the Grand Prix!
Mavis is waving her purse! Somebody get that toad a trophy!
What a race! Pratt Street will be talking about this for years!
Close one! Second place, but the crowd still loves him!

poe_night: The fog rolls in off the harbor, and the old graveyard goes quiet.
Lamplight flickers over stones older than anyone in the city.
Somewhere behind the church wall, a black bird shuffles its feathers.
They say on cold nights a poet still walks these narrow paths.
Footsteps on the gravel. Harold stops. The footsteps stop too.
A raven's shadow crosses the moon and lands on a crooked cross.
Under the church, the old catacombs breathe out a chill.
Someone left a rose here last year. It hasn't wilted.
The wind spells out a name in the dry leaves. Then forgets it.
A heartbeat? No. Just Harold's cane tapping the stone. Right?
Every gravestone leans a little closer when you're not looking.
The bell tower creaks midnight, though the bell has been gone for years.
Three roses, one bottle, one toad. The old tradition holds.
Dawn comes gray over Westminster, and the shadows slip back underground.

catch: Striped bass! A fine harbor fish, about 18 inches.
White perch! Small but feisty. Into the bucket.
Blue crab on the line! Careful, he's grabbing back.
Catfish! Whiskers and all. He looks unimpressed.
An eel! Slippery, wiggly, and very annoyed.
Croaker! He's croaking louder than Harold.
rare: RARE! A golden blue crab with a tiny crown!
RARE! A sturgeon, older than the Constellation!
RARE! The legendary harbor eel nobody believes in!
chompy_taunts: Chompy: Those are MY crabs, toad. Hands off!
Chompy: Clack clack! Come closer, I dare you.
Chompy: I've snapped bigger canes than yours.
Chompy: This pier's mine. Fish somewhere else!
Chompy: You hook me? Ha! I'll hook YOU.
Chompy: Bring your seasoning, old timer. Not for me!

hawker_lines: Crab cakes! All lump, no filler, hon!
Pit beef sliced thin, piled high! Step right up!
Coddies! Two for a dollar, three if you smile!
Fresh lake trout, fried up hot! Don't ask what kind of trout!
Cookies the size of your hat, sweetie!
Lemon sticks! Peppermint in a lemon, trust me!
Oysters on the half shell, shucked while you wait!
Pickles! Sour, half sour, or so sour you'll whistle!
Hey Harold! Your usual? Extra horseradish?
Market's open, folks! Come hungry, leave happy!

celebration_crowd: I can sit on my stoop again, hon!
Kids, you can play outside again!
Best day this street's had in years!
Get that toad a crab cake!
I knew he could do it!
Let's hear it for the old folks!
Who's next? He's on a roll!
